title: an instance seal swaps on a disk, not on a tmpfs, unless its caller names a temp dir
intention: An instance seal makes its pristine snapshot and swap on a disk-backed directory unless its caller names one, so two seals at once never fill a RAM-backed /tmp.
why: Law 4 (a rule that matters is physics, not policy) and Law 3: on akiendelllinux /tmp is a 7.7G tmpfs; isolation.py:459 and :498 make the pristine snapshot and the seal swap with tempfile.mkdtemp, which honours TMPDIR and otherwise lands on /tmp; each seal copies ~1.4G (cairn-instance-pristine-* 685M + cairn-instance-seal-* 685M). At 08:2x a seal from akienasus's 0da9 prove (pid 2071739, swap under /tmp) and a sealed --exec of mine with no TMPDIR ran together and the second died 'No space left on device' in snapshot_instance_space. The processes that start seals without a caller's export carry no TMPDIR: the live bus (pid 2083024, cairn.devices.cairn.machines.bus serve), the ground loop (pid 9567) and every superclaude session (/proc/<pid>/environ), because remote.py:323 and shim.py:191 launch units through systemd-run carrying only CAIRN_*, HOME and PATH. With TMPDIR=/var/tmp (ext4, 765G free) a 21-proof reseal plus a 2-proof seal left /tmp flat at 2.1G free over 13 samples 30 s apart (/home/akien/.cairn/devices/cc/0/scratch/akiendelllinux_cc_0/tmpwatch/samples.txt).
how: isolation.py chooses its swap root once: the caller's TMPDIR when set, else a disk-backed dir it owns (e.g. /var/tmp, checked not tmpfs, else ~/.cairn/devices/tester/0/temp/), and passes dir= to both mkdtemp calls and to line 374's root. The proof drives the chooser over a scratch mountinfo/temp layout for clauses 1 and 3, and runs two seals at once under a scratch small tmpfs default for clause 2 (or a sized fake that refuses a write past its cap, if a tmpfs mount is not available unprivileged).

clauses.claim: with TMPDIR unset, an instance seal's pristine snapshot and swap are made on a directory that is not a tmpfs (read from /proc/self/mountinfo for the swap's path)
with TMPDIR unset and a tmpfs mounted at the default temp dir with less free space than one snapshot, two concurrent instance seals both complete
with TMPDIR set by the caller, the swap is made under it, as today

decisions.text: D1: isolation.py picks one swap root (caller's TMPDIR, else a disk-backed dir it checks is not tmpfs) and every mkdtemp and line 374's root use it.
D2: a new proof, one tooth per clause, over scratch layouts.
